judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, resolved Grade rank 1, gap 0). B2.5.9.1 'Understand simple sentences in writing' (Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage, Sub-Strand 9 Using Simple and Compound Sentences; bounded indicator 'Identify the structure of simple sentences') addresses sentence-internal grammatical structure, while B2.4.7.2 'Matching parts of sentences to composition' (Strand 4 Writing, Sub-Strand 7 Controlled Writing; bounded indicator 'Re-arrange jumbled sentences logically' within a retold story) addresses assembling and ordering sentences into a coherent composition. These are substantively coherent, complementary sentence-level writing skills taught within the same grade and mutually reinforcing across the grammar and writing strands, which supports symmetric relatesTo. The evidence does not show a pair-specific extension, deepening, or dependency at equal rank: knowledge of simple-sentence structure is not demonstrated by the bounded text to be what enables logical re-ordering of whole sentences, so buildsTowards in either direction is not supported, and the coherence is more than generic repetition or shared wording, so no_relation is not warranted. Nomination signals (shared BASIC 2 ancestor, rank proximity, weak 'b2' code prefix, single shared token 'sentences', trigram overlap) carry no semantic weight on their own. Material limitation: both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and every node carries upstream audit/merge/code context, including a merged BASIC 2 grade organizer, so this judgment rests only on the bounded statement text, hierarchy, and source-context labels supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same grade rank 0, same statement-type grain). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 1 Indicators (rank 0, same grain), so no rank-based developmental direction is available. First (B1.5.10.1.2, Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage, Sub-Strand 10 Spelling, under 'Use phonics knowledge to spell words') asks learners to fill in blank spaces in simple words, a phonics-driven letter/word-level encoding task. Second (B1.4.4.1.1, Strand 4 Writing, Sub-Strand 4 Labelling Items, under 'Draw and label simple objects') asks learners to draw pictures and use invented spelling to write about themselves, an emergent composing/labelling task whose LCs are 'draw simple pictures of peers or various objects' and 'use invented spelling to write about oneself'. They cohere substantively around early encoding of words in writing (accurate spelling of simple words vs. approximate/invented spelling in self-directed writing), which is meaningful complementary reinforcement across strands. However, invented spelling explicitly tolerates non-conventional forms and the drawing/labelling focus is distinct, so the evidence does not establish that proficiency in either task supports success in the other; symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Shared parent-grade, weak token/trigram overlap ('simple', 'spelling' tag) and code prefix 'b1' alone were not treated as semantic evidence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting exemplar-level detail.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 3 Indicators (rank 2, identical canonical grade coordinate) within Strand 1: Oral Language, but under different Sub-Strands and different Content Standards: B3.1.9.1.1 'Give and respond to commands, instructions and directions' (Sub-Strand 9, giving/responding to commands) and B3.1.8.1.2 'Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering the inversion questions' (Sub-Strand 8, asking/answering questions). Their Learning Components confirm complementary rather than dependent skills: producing and responding to directives versus prosodic control (pronunciation/intonation) when initiating and answering inversion questions. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators (rank 2, same grade coordinate) under Strand 2: Reading, but in different Sub-Strands: B3.2.5.1.1 'Use consonant blends to build words' sits under Sub-Strand 5 (Blends and Consonant Clusters) with Content Standard B3.2.5.1 (identify and use consonant blends), while B3.2.3.1.2 'Use words containing digraphs to make meaningful sentences' sits under Sub-Strand 3 (Word Families, Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs) with Content Standard B3.2.3.1 (rhyming endings and digraphs for comprehension). They are complementary letter-pattern phonics skills (blends vs digraphs) applied at different linguistic levels (word building vs sentence construction), giving substantive conceptual coherence within Basic 3 phonics/word-recognition work, but the shared tokens ('use', 'words') and page/code proximity are weak signals and the two target distinct grapheme sets, so neither same-rank direction is substantively supported as a developmental dependency. Evidence is bounded: source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC metadata are truncated, and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context.
